rendered: Prodigiosin synthesis in S. marcescens is strongly temperature-dependent:Production is strongly temperature-dependent, peaking at 25–28 ◦C and suppressed at ≥37 ◦C[1]. This is the phenotype shown schematically inFig. 2[2], panel A, where the plate at the lower temperature range bears pigmented colonies and the hotter plate is pale[3]. Mechanistically, the loss of pigment at higher temperature is attributed todecreased expression and stability of PigF and PigN at higher temperatures[4], and engineering of the corresponding mRNA half-lives together with designed disulfide bonds in PigF raised yields at both of the cultivation temperatures tested[5].
